transport: RS-485 over RJ45, and CAN, both confirmed present by the vendor manual for the LifePower4 48V. Framing, baud and addressing for the V2 revision specifically: not established.
gotchas: DIALECT UNKNOWN. Three EG4 battery protocols exist and no source ties the V2 revision to one of them at better than single-implementation confidence.

The only model-specific claim found is wombatt's README line: 'EG4 Lifepower v2 (BMS Type: lifepowerv2) (protocol switches: 1-off, 2 thru 6-on)', and in wombatt's bms.go `lifepowerv2` resolves to `NewEG4LLv2()` with the comment 'Same protocol as EG4LLv2 BMS' — i.e. the eg4-ll-modbus register map. One implementation. No

Contradicting that, the same README routes plain 'EG4 Lifepower' to EG4LLv2 as well, while EG4's own document titled 'LifePower4 Battery Communication Protocol' describes the HEX-ASCII 0x4A protocol, and slim-bean's sniff of EG4's BMS tool against a LifePower4 shows a third, group-framed protocol. Three sources, three

What is missing to resolve this: a vendor document that names the V2 revision, or a second independent implementation confirming which DIP combination selects which framing. Until then a driver author must sniff the bench unit.

The V1 manual (EG4-Lifepower4-48V-Manual-2.4.0) has no LCD and therefore no protocol-selection menu — DIP switches are the only selector, and the manual documents them for ADDRESS only, never for protocol. Whatever wombatt's 'switches 1-off, 2 thru 6-on' does is undocumented by the vendor.
